title: US-South Korea Formally Wrap Up Ulchi Freedom Shield Drill Six Days Early
detail: The US and South Korean militaries formally concluded the Ulchi Freedom Shield command post exercise on Friday, August 21, 2026, six days ahead of its original August 27 end date, after President Trump ordered the Pentagon on August 16 to 'substantially reduce' the drill's duration and scale, citing his personal relationship with Kim Jong-un and separately voicing frustration with Seoul over the Iran war. The shortened schedule meant only the first, defense-focused phase was completed; the second, counteroffensive-focused phase was skipped, and roughly half of the 14 planned joint field training exercises — including river-crossing drills along the Imjin River in Paju, Gyeonggi Province — were cancelled or converted to simulations, according to South Korean commanders and a Pentagon spokesperson cited by Reuters. South Korea's military confirmed simply that 'the Ulchi Freedom Shield, a command post exercise with the U.S., ended on Friday,' with the cancelled exercises expected to be rescheduled after further Seoul-Washington consultations. Pyongyang had already signaled the gesture would not change its posture (Kim Yo-jong, Aug 18) and answered with a 10-missile barrage the day before the drill ended (Aug 20) — see those events for details.
